laya is free and open source. If it helps you, sponsor the work on GitHub . 

 

 New in 0.5: laya reads images, audio and video, takes 73k tokens, says when it should not decide, and keeps learning. All open source under Apache 2.0 ( pip install -U laya ).

- Text, images, audio and video. agent.predict(...) with image= , audio= or video= gives the same typed answers as for text.
- 73,728 tokens of context. Whole contracts, threads and logs in one read.
- Abstain and unbound , explained below.
- Physics, not text generation. Each candidate answer is a valley; the input is a particle that rolls and settles in one. Deterministic, constant cost, nothing generated.
- Any LLM as the reader. One small decision engine on top of a frozen reader, from 0.8B to 27B.
- Continuous learning. from laya import Learner : it answers from day one and learns from every answer your team confirms, on your own machine, in seconds on a CPU with no fine-tuning.
- A teacher for what it is unsure of. laya.Escalator(learner, teacher) sends only the records it abstains on, finds unbound or is not yet sure of to your teacher (a review queue, a rules engine, or a model you serve yourself with laya.vllm teacher ), serves that answer and learns from it, so the teacher is needed less and less. Guide.

 How abstain and unbound work

The input is placed as a particle in a small decision space where every candidate answer is a valley. Where the particle settles, and how deep, is the answer and its probability.

- abstain : it declines to commit. The threshold is calibrated so that, among the answers it does give, the error rate stays under the configured risk (10% by default).
- prediction set : the conformal set, every option the answer could still be at alpha 0.10. One option means it is sure; two or more means the input really is ambiguous.
- unbound : the particle settled far from every valley, so the input looks unlike anything it knows (likely off-distribution). It is reported on every answer but does not route on its own: measured, it also fired on 71% of normal banking77 rows, so it would have sent most good answers to review.
- route : what to do with it, auto or review . Without labels, review when it abstains or the set holds more than one option. With labels ( agent.fit / agent.calibrate ), a band placed where precision holds at 95% on your rows decides. Gate on route , never on a confidence number.

 Benchmarks at a glance

 Continuous learning. 14 decision templates (31 questions), each starting from about 600 generated examples, then learning from confirmed answers; scored on 60 held-out rows per template.

 day one after 40 confirmed answers after 120 
 --- --- --- --- 
 laya, laya.Learner 84.7% 91.6% 96.0% 
 Jev 1.14, confirmed answers written into its criteria 89.5% 91.5% 92.6% 

Jev leads on day one (23 of 31 questions); they are level at 40; laya leads at 120 (12 wins, 7 losses, 12 ties). Jev cannot be taught, only prompted, and is a hosted API (364 ms a request from India).

 What learning costs. laya learns from 300 answers in 34 s on 8 CPU threads, with no GPU (0.72 s an answer, 6.4 GB of RAM; on a GPU 40 ms and 2 GB). Fine-tuning the classic encoder on the same 300 rows takes 89 s on a GPU with 9 GB and rewrites all 421M weights.

 Learning from a stream, November 2026 (4B reader, held-out rows):

 laya Jev 1.14 
 --- --- --- 
 banking77, 924 held out, after 4,928 rows 87.5% , ECE 0.028, 92.5% routed auto at 91.5% precision 79.4% as shipped (ECE 0.078), 85.7% with examples 
 typed-decisions, 2,000 decisions, after 1,200 rows 73.7%, ECE 0.031 74.7%, ECE 0.047 (level) 

 Across readers , one byte-identical decision engine, 50,676 held-out records: 0.8B 76.5%, 4B 79.1%, 27B 81.1%, ECE 0.010 to 0.021.

 Where it loses. Zero-shot on generic public suites a large hosted model leads. As a prompt-injection gate on real traffic (ToxicChat, 1.8% attacks), Jev untaught catches 79.1% at 0.3% refused against 73.0% at 0.7% for a fitted head. The benchmarks further down are for the classic encoder checkpoints.

 Under the hood the new engine comes from vegaml, installed with laya. For the classic encoder, name it ( laya.Agent("convaiinnovations/laya") ) or pass vegaml=False . 

 Studio, from Embedding Space builds the starting set for your questions and runs it for you.

 Cite this work. M, N.; M, A. From Laya to Vega: Open Non-Autoregressive Decision Models with Calibrated Probabilities. Preprints 2026 , 2026110781. 

 
 BibTeX 

 

 

 Multilingual, non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine. Typed decisions over 100+ languages in a single forward pass — 33 ms — trained with reinforcement learning against strictly proper scoring rules (RLCD), with a router that picks the right checkpoint per request.

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 

 Installation

 

With uv, run uv add laya in a uv project or uv pip install laya in a virtual environment.

Python 3.10 or newer. Optional extras: laya[serve] (HTTP server), laya[mcp] (MCP server), laya[langchain] (LangChain and LangGraph), laya[llamaindex] (LlamaIndex selectors), laya[crewai] (CrewAI routing), laya[onnx] (ONNX Runtime), laya[fast] (TileLang GPU fast path), laya[structured] (pydantic models in decide ), laya[vision] (Pillow and torchvision, for predict(image=...) and predict(video=...) ), laya[audio] (soundfile, to decode audio files). Step-by-step setup for each platform, CPU-only or GPU PyTorch builds, and troubleshooting are in Installation details.

For TypeScript / Node.js / browser, see laya-ts/ . npm releases ( npm install laya-ts ) are published from this repository's laya-ts-v release tags.

 Long documents. laya-multilingual reads up to 8,192 tokens with max len=8192 . Measured accuracy and time by document length, reproducible with research/scripts/bench long context.py :

usage.title: Minimal example (30 seconds)
usage.html:
from laya import Router

router = Router()  # downloads only the selected checkpoint on first use
result = router.predict(
    {"body": "We were billed twice. Please refund the duplicate."},
    {"billing": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the user request a refund?"}},
)
print(result["answers"]["billing"]["noul"])  # P(true), a float from 0.0 to 1.0
print(result["routing"]["model"])            # which checkpoint answered, e.g. 'english'

Input is any state (str, dict, or list — text, email, ticket, JSON document) plus a dict of typed questions (choice = pick one label, score = ordinal levels, noul = yes/no statement check). Each result["answers"][qid] is an answer dict: choice is the selected label, score is the expected ordinal level, and noul is P(true). confidence is a separate field in that dict; probabilities is available for choice and score. result["routing"] explains which checkpoint was picked and why. Values depend on the checkpoint and input. For ready-made question sets see laya.presets (triage_questions, moderation_questions, email_questions, ...).

Full walkthrough:

from laya import Router

# Preload checkpoints into memory for instant sub-35ms routing
router = Router(preload=True)

# 1. State in any language or schema
state = {
    "from": "user@acme.com",
    "subject": "Duplicate charge on invoice #4411",
    "body": "Hi, we were billed twice for March. Please refund the duplicate today or we will cancel our plan."
}

# 2. Define your typed questions
questions = {
    "department": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Which department should handle this request?",
        "criteria": {
            "billing": "invoices, payments, refunds",
            "technical": "bugs, outages, system errors",
            "sales": "pricing, new contracts, plan upgrades",
            "other": "everything else"
        }
    },
    "urgency": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How urgent is this request?",
        "criteria": ["not urgent", "soon", "critical deadline or blocking issue"]
    },
    "churn_risk": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the user threaten to cancel or leave?"
    },
    "refund_requested": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does the user explicitly request a refund?"
    }
}

# 3. English state -> automatically routed to laya (ModernBERT-large, 39.5 ms)
res_en = router.predict(state, questions)
print("Department :", res_en["answers"]["department"]["choice"])  # -> billing (confidence: 0.94)
print("Routing    :", res_en["routing"]["model"])                 # -> english

# 4. Hindi state -> automatically routed to laya-multilingual (mmBERT-base, 32.8 ms)
res_hi = router.predict({"body": "मुझसे दो बार शुल्क लिया गया, कृपया पैसे वापस करें।"}, questions)
print("Department :", res_hi["answers"]["department"]["choice"])  # -> billing (confidence: 0.86)
print("Routing    :", res_hi["routing"]["model"])                 # -> multilingual

# 5. Explicit override when you want a specific checkpoint
res_td = router.predict(state, questions, model="typed-decisions")

Every result carries full routing metadata explaining why the choice was made:

res_hi["routing"]
# {
#   'model': 'multilingual',
#   'repo': 'convaiinnovations/laya/multilingual',
#   'reason': 'non-Latin script (devanagari, 100% of letters); the English checkpoint cannot read it',
#   'detection': {'script': 'devanagari', 'script_profile': {'devanagari': 1.0},
#                 'language': None, 'is_english': False, 'language_undecided': True,
#                 'diacritic_rate': 0.0, 'non_latin_fraction': 1.0, 'mixed_segment': None},
#   'workflow': None
# }

All five keys are always present. detection is the laya.lang.analyse result the decision was made from, and is None whenever routing decided before detection ran: model=, task=, a detected workflow, a decisive lang= and a resolving lang_guess all take precedence over it and short-circuit it. workflow names the typed-decisions workflow whose question ids matched, and is None when none did.

Inspect a routing decision without running any forward pass:

router.route({"body": "Der Kunde wurde zweimal belastet"}, questions).reason
# "Latin script but language looks like 'de', not English"

Very short Latin-script text often carries nothing that identifies its language ("Quero cancelar", "Esqueci minha senha"). Such text goes to default, which is "multilingual" since 0.4.0. Text the detector can place is unaffected: identified English still goes to the English checkpoint.

router = Router()                                                   # default="multilingual"
router.route({"body": "Esqueci minha senha"}).model                 # -> multilingual
router.route({"body": "Please refund the duplicate charge"}).model  # -> english

If most of your traffic is English, set it back. The English checkpoint scores 0.820 on English against the multilingual checkpoint's 0.710, and the break-even is around 62% English traffic:

router = Router(default="english")

Running one of the shipped servers rather than your own Router, the same setting is LAYA_DEFAULT_MODEL=english — in the environment of laya-serve, the MCP server or the laya-serve container (docs/docker.md). It is the routing fallback only: text the detector can place is routed on what it detects, whatever this is set to.
